identity.field: Peer-owned private field brand and direct exact instance/activation/native lifetime owner
identity.resident: Private resident payload owner must match the same exact instance/activation/native lifetime before field binding
identity.builder: Private mint, one bound field, strongly registered in the exact instance before exposure
identity.fragment: Exact private field, fragment object, u64 offset and fixed length; no structural byte provider
identity.token: Private copied/cancelled mint with exact fragment, field, builder, offset and length
identity.release: Peer-owned private receipt must bind the issued token and exact fragment

storage.admission: Reserve full page bytes and owner slot in the composition-shared pool before fixed allocation
storage.index: One bounded linked cell per admitted page; no full field allocation or concatenation
storage.reader: Private sequential reader is strongly registered before exposure; it never exposes a page buffer
storage.consumer: Concrete typed decoder owns the issued reader; close drains issued readers before payload pages
storage.arithmetic: Validate all source offsets and declared lengths as u64, then use bigint for cumulative offsets; numeric page offsets remain within 256

rules: Only one current fragment is accepted; failed offer leaves the source unchanged
Each step performs one child operation or one fixed transition, preserving refused/rejected child counts
Rejected or throwing copy/source children permanently fault the producer, including after partial mutation; bounded close remains serviceable
A throwing scalar read cannot advance its offset or silently resume; the registered reader remains owned until explicit close
The private constructor installs its builder in the reserved parent before finalization or binding; close checks actual private source binding rather than a lost success return
A raw fragment is copied to independently owned destination storage and released before the next raw page is required
Capacity refusal retains the exact current fragment and partial destination; it neither requests another raw page nor invents resident credit
Copy success requires all offered bytes written and all source byte readers detached
Cancellation detaches source readers and issues distinct cancelled evidence; partial destination remains owned until bounded retirement
Copied/cancelled evidence is retained until the exact peer release receipt, including retry after send refusal
Only the builder drives the original field continuation after copied receipt settlement, forwarding one child turn without wrapper charge
A consumed partial fragment with no actual next fragment remains blocked; no offset, page, fragment or InputAck is synthesized
Finish requires exact declared length and no outstanding input fragment or release receipt
An abandoned or throwing caller cannot erase the instance's strong builder/read ownership
Revocation rejects new admissions but does not revoke captured close or input-release authority
Final instance retirement requires source obligations, issued readers, destination pages and owner roster cells terminal
No capacity default, maxPatchBytes-derived allowance, physical-heap assertion or UI publication acknowledgement is introduced
